q: Who is commonly called the Father of Artificial Intelligence?
explain: John McCarthy was a founding AI researcher and is commonly called the Father of AI.

q: The Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, a founding event of AI as a discipline, took place in:
explain: The Dartmouth workshop was held in 1956; the proposal using the term 'artificial intelligence' dated from 31 August 1955.

q: Which branch of AI learns patterns from data?
explain: Machine Learning is the AI branch that learns patterns from data; deep learning is ML with many-layered neural networks.

q: Deep learning is best described as:
options: ML using neural networks with multiple processing layers
explain: Deep learning uses neural networks with several processing layers and is a branch of machine learning.

q: Logic Theorist, one of the earliest AI programs that proved mathematical theorems, was developed in 1956 by:
explain: Allen Newell, Herbert A. Simon and J. C. Shaw created Logic Theorist, which ran on RAND's JOHNNIAC computer.

q: LISP, an influential language for symbolic AI, was developed by John McCarthy in:
explain: LISP (List Processing) dates to 1958; ELIZA's landmark paper appeared in 1966.

q: The early chatbot ELIZA, which used keywords and scripted response rules, was developed by:
explain: Joseph Weizenbaum of MIT created ELIZA, and the landmark paper came out in 1966.

q: Which language preceded LISP and was used for Logic Theorist?
explain: IPL came before LISP, which is why LISP is called an early influential AI language rather than unconditionally the first.

q: Sophia, the humanoid robot granted Saudi Arabian citizenship in 2017, was made by:
explain: Sophia is a humanoid robot made by Hanson Robotics; Saudi Arabia announced citizenship for it in 2017.

q: IBM Watson became famous for winning which televised contest, in 2011?
options: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
explain: Watson, IBM's question-answering system, won Jeopardy! in 2011; watsonx was announced in 2023.

q: Claude, the AI chatbot, was developed by:
explain: Claude is from Anthropic (March 2023). ChatGPT is OpenAI's, Grok is xAI's and Meta AI belongs to Meta.

q: Grok is a chatbot developed by:
explain: Grok comes from xAI and was introduced in November 2023.

q: Google's chatbot Bard was renamed Gemini in:
explain: Gemini models arrived in December 2023, but the Bard-to-Gemini chatbot renaming was in February 2024.

q: Which pairing of assistant and company is correct?
explain: Alexa is Amazon's, Siri is Apple's, Cortana is Microsoft's and Watson is IBM's.

q: Cortana's announcement with Windows Phone 8.1 happened in:
explain: Microsoft announced Cortana with Windows Phone 8.1 in 2014; Siri's iPhone 4S integration was in 2011.

q: What does GPT stand for in ChatGPT?
explain: GPT means Generative Pre-trained Transformer; 'Chat' just describes the conversational interface.

q: ChatGPT was publicly introduced on:
explain: OpenAI publicly introduced ChatGPT on 30 November 2022.

q: In basic exam categories, ChatGPT is classified as:
explain: ChatGPT is treated as Narrow AI powered by large language models; it should not be described as Super AI.

q: Which field of AI deals with processing and generating human language, the area ChatGPT works in?
explain: NLP concerns processing and generating human language, central to ChatGPT.

q: OpenAI was announced in:
explain: OpenAI was announced in December 2015; Microsoft's expanded partnership came in January 2023.

q: Who published foundational research on secure digital timestamping in 1991, an early step towards blockchain?
options: Stuart Haber and W. Scott Stornetta
explain: Haber and Stornetta published the 1991 timestamping research; Satoshi Nakamoto presented Bitcoin in 2008.

q: The Bitcoin network began operating in which year?
explain: The Bitcoin proposal came in 2008 and the network began operating in 2009.

q: Which statement about Bitcoin and blockchain is correct?
options: Blockchain is an application and Bitcoin is the technology
Bitcoin is an application; blockchain is the record-keeping technology
They are exactly the same thing
Blockchain was invented only in 2009 by Satoshi alone
explain: Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency application built on blockchain, and earlier research from 1991 means Satoshi was not the sole inventor of the ideas.

q: In a blockchain, successive blocks are linked by:
options: Hash values of the previous block
explain: Each block stores the previous block's hash, which creates the cryptographic link and lets changes to earlier data be detected.

q: The first block of a blockchain, which has no preceding block, is called the:
explain: The genesis block is the first block and has no previous block.

q: Which blockchain network type restricts access and participation to an organisation?
explain: Private networks are controlled by an organisation; public ones are broadly open and hybrid ones mix public and private features.

q: Which of the following is NOT a defining feature of a decentralised blockchain?
explain: A decentralised public blockchain has no single central ledger authority; centralised control is not a defining feature.

q: Which statement about blockchain immutability is most accurate?
options: It guarantees no change is ever possible
It means blockchain can never be attacked
It means strong resistance to alteration under normal operation, not an absolute guarantee
explain: Immutability means altering accepted history is very hard, but blockchain is not automatically attack-proof.

q: Who is widely credited with introducing the term Internet of Things in 1999?
explain: Kevin Ashton used the phrase in a Procter & Gamble presentation about RFID-based supply chains.

q: RFID stands for:
explain: RFID is Radio Frequency Identification, where the R means Radio; it identifies tagged objects using radio communication.

q: In 1982, Carnegie Mellon students connected which device to ARPANET, an early IoT example?
explain: The CMU Coke machine (1982) came before the internet-controlled toaster of 1990 (John Romkey and Simon Hackett).

q: Which statement about an RFID tag is correct?
options: It always has its own internet connection
It does not automatically have its own internet connection; readers and connected systems provide the link
explain: A tag identifies objects by radio; readers and connected systems link it to the internet.

q: In an IoT system, which component carries out physical actions such as operating a valve or switch?
explain: Actuators perform physical actions, while sensors collect information about the physical world.

q: Which protocol provides TLS-style protection for datagram communication, commonly over UDP?
explain: DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) protects datagram traffic; IPsec works at the IP network layer.

q: Which statement about 5G and IoT is correct?
options: 5G is the broader concept of connected physical objects
5G is a connectivity technology; IoT is the broader concept of connected physical objects
IoT is a generation of mobile networks
5G and IoT mean the same thing
explain: 5G is fifth-generation mobile communication technology, while IoT covers connected physical objects in general.

q: Which of the following is true about a self-driving vehicle?
options: It is always an IoT system
It is automatically IoT only because it is automated
It is not automatically IoT merely because it is automated; connectivity and data exchange matter
It is IoT only if it uses a standalone GPS receiver
explain: Automation alone does not make something IoT; the object must be connected and exchange data.

q: MQTT is a lightweight messaging protocol that uses which model?
explain: In MQTT a publisher sends messages, a broker forwards them, and subscribers interested in the topic receive them.

q: IIoT refers to:
explain: IIoT is Industrial Internet of Things: connected sensors, machines and software applied to industrial operations.

q: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is mainly useful for:
options: Battery-operated devices such as fitness trackers and wireless sensors
explain: BLE is designed for very low power use, extending operating time between battery changes or charges.

q: What is the status of the MQTT name in the current standard?
options: It officially expands to Message Queuing Telemetry Transport
It officially expands to Machine Query Transfer Tool
It uses MQTT as the protocol name with no official expansion
It stands for Mobile Quick Transfer Technology
explain: Message Queuing Telemetry Transport is a common exam expansion; historically it was MQ Telemetry Transport, and the standard now has no official expansion.
